reason: The quote states stopped Spot Instances start only if Spot capacity is still available within the maximum price and that Spot evaluates capacity every time they are started.

The quote supports that running Spot Instances can be stopped and kept for later use and that 'Stop is available for persistent Spot requests'; it never says 'only', so the claim's 'available only for persistent Spot requests' is stronger than the quote.

The quote recommends multiple Spot capacity pools to maximize available Spot capacity and names EC2 Auto Scaling, EC2 Fleet and Spot Fleet as the automation that finds cost-effective capacity across pools.
The quotes support 1152 vCPUs for Standard, 128 vCPUs for P and the lower start for new accounts; the claim's 128 vCPUs for F, G, Inf and X come only from context rows that are not quoted.
The quote states a stopped instance has no hourly usage or data transfer charge but EBS volume storage is still charged.
The quote states T2 instances can be purchased as On-Demand, Reserved or Spot Instances.
The quote states a T2 instance with a zero CPU credit balance remains at baseline CPU performance; the standard-mode qualifier only narrows the scope.
The quote states Trainium and Inferentia are purpose built for deep learning and generative AI and save up to 50% on training and inference costs over comparable EC2 instances.
The quote recommends, as a general best practice, launching Spot and On-Demand fleets with EC2 Auto Scaling because of its additional fleet management features.

The quotes state that with Capacity Rebalancing enabled a rebalance recommendation launches a new Spot Instance before the at-risk one is interrupted, and that it is available only for fleets of type maintain.
The quote states a fleet can launch Spot and On-Demand Instances and that Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts apply with the On-Demand Instances in the fleet.

The quotes state price capacity optimized is the best choice for most Spot workloads, lowest price is not recommended because of the highest interruption risk, and lowest price is the AWS CLI default.
The quote states both have the same core functionality, EC2 Fleet is command line only without console support, and Spot Fleet has console support but a legacy API with no planned investment.

The quote supports 100 GB free data transfer out per month aggregated across services and Regions except China and GovCloud; the claim's rate-tier sentence is unquoted context, and the quote says 'AWS customers', not 'per account' as the scope says.

The quote gives both rules: accounts before July 15, 2025 and under 12 months old get t2.micro (or t3.micro) within limits; accounts on or after that date get the six listed types for 6 months or until credits are used up.
The quotes state Global View shows some resources in one or many Regions in a single console with global search, and does not let you modify resources in any way.
The quote states Graviton-powered EC2 instances deliver up to 40% better price performance than comparable non-Graviton instances.

The quote supports recompiling C, C++ and GoLang for Arm, but it limits the minimal-change statement to interpreted-language apps 'not reliant on native CPU instruction sets', a condition the claim drops.
The quote states M6g and A1 instances need arm64 AMIs and x86 AMIs are not compatible with them.
The quote states a hibernated instance cannot be modified, unlike a stopped non-hibernated instance whose instance type or size can be changed.
Under the EBS volume type prerequisite, the quote states the volumes must use gp2, gp3, io1 or io2, which matches 'supports only'.
The quote states hibernation is enabled for On-Demand or Spot Instances at launch and cannot be enabled on an existing running or stopped instance.
The quote states hibernation for more than 60 days is not supported and gives the start, stop and start steps to keep the instance longer.
The quotes state hibernating instances pay standard EBS storage rates with no instance usage fee, as with a stopped instance, and associated Elastic IP addresses are still charged.
The quote states an instance in an Auto Scaling group or used by ECS cannot be hibernated and that Auto Scaling marks it unhealthy and might replace it.
The quotes state Linux instances over 150 GiB of RAM and Windows instances over 16 GiB of RAM cannot be hibernated.
The quotes state the root volume must be an EBS volume, not instance store, and must be encrypted.
The quote states hibernation suspends to disk, saving RAM to the EBS root volume, and on start the root volume is restored, RAM reloaded and the instance ID kept.

The quotes state the Spot request must be persistent with no launch group, an EC2-hibernated Spot Instance can be resumed only by EC2, and only when capacity is available and the Spot price is at or below the maximum price.

The quotes support the supported-family rule, no bare metal, all Regions and the general purpose list (T2 to T8i); the compute, memory and storage optimized families and the Graviton C and R families come only from unquoted context lines.
The quote states instances on the same physical host are isolated as though on separate hosts and the hypervisor isolates CPU and memory.
The quote gives the common pattern: Savings Plans for baseline, On-Demand or Spot for fluctuating workloads, On-Demand Capacity Reservations for mission-critical capacity assurance.
The quote states IAM roles let applications make API requests from instances without managing their credentials, instead of creating and distributing AWS credentials.
The quotes state only one IAM role can be attached to an instance, the same role can be attached to many instances, and an instance profile contains only one role.
The quotes state the role credentials are temporary and rotated automatically, and that SDKs, the AWS CLI and applications on the instance get them automatically from the instance metadata service.
The quotes state the account default can be set per Region to IMDSv2 so new instances launch with HttpTokens required and hop limit 2, and that existing instances are not affected.
The quotes state IMDSv2 can be enforced per account and Region, instances launch only if configured to require IMDSv2 regardless of instance or AMI configuration, and otherwise the launch fails.

The quote gives 169.254.169.254 and fd00:ec2::254 but says you must 'enable and use' the IPv6 address; the claim drops that enable condition, and the Nitro and IPv6-subnet condition is in the unquoted next sentence.
The quote states an AMI registered or modified with imds-support v2.0 launches instances with IMDSv2 and hop limit 2; the precedence qualifier matches the page's order-of-precedence section.
The quotes state by default either IMDSv1 or IMDSv2 or both can be used, and IMDS can be set per instance to accept only IMDSv2, which makes IMDSv1 calls fail.
